disposition_reason: Table 2 prints mean ± SD Pb, As and Cu and non-detected Cd in powdered pepper from six Kwara State markets and a laboratory control.

study.design: Market survey of commercial powdered pepper (aflatoxins and metals)
study.market: Offa, Oja-Oba, Ganmo, Shao, Elemere and Malete markets, Kwara State, Nigeria
study.method: ICP-MS (PerkinElmer ELAN DRC-e); sample digestion not described

findings.group: laboratory-prepared control (fresh pepper from an Ilorin market, powdered in the laboratory)
findings.notes: Commercial powdered pepper (200 g) from Kwara State markets; ICP-MS (PerkinElmer ELAN DRC-e). Table 2 values are mean ± SD (n=3 replicate determinations). Digestion, LOD and QA not described. Basis as sold (powder).

findings.group: laboratory-prepared control (fresh pepper from an Ilorin market, powdered in the laboratory)
findings.notes: Commercial powdered pepper (200 g) from Kwara State markets; ICP-MS (PerkinElmer ELAN DRC-e). Table 2 values are mean ± SD (n=3 replicate determinations). Digestion, LOD and QA not described. Basis as sold (powder). Arsenic at 10-23 mg/kg is very high for pepper and the method section lists the analyte as "Ar"; no speciation (total arsenic).

unresolved: Hg is listed as an analyte in the method but no Hg results are reported.

The introduction sentence that pepper samples "were not contaminated with heavy metals (cadmium, iron, lead, zinc, cobalt, and chromium)" refers to an earlier study (Farombi et al., 2020), not to these samples; the paper itself reports Pb, As and Cu and no detectable Cd.
Text says Ganmo had the highest Pb (3.45 mg/kg) and states mean As 12.01 mg/kg; Table 2 gives Ganmo 6.25 and mean As 17.12. Table values recorded with a flag.
